Financial Advising Firms to be Required to Act with Fiduciary Duty

The goal of the new rule is to make money managers contractually obligated to put their clients first, rather than simply be encouraged to do so.

This is somehow a bad thing? And a new idea? The fuck.

It sounds superficially good, but has undesirable side effects. Fiduciary duty is a massive legal hurdle that carries high costs (seen the costs for medical care or hiring an attorney lately?). So it protects people who don't bother to look at the costs on the front freaking page for their investments, and harms people who do their own due diligence and want to minimize their costs for investments.

The whole financial advising industry scares me. I used to work for a financial planning software company in IT. The training required that I went through 6 weeks of financial advice boot camp so I understood what I was talking about when I had financial advisers on the phone and had to help them with our product.

Some of the questions they asked me were frightening. They were managing lots of peoples money, using our software and yet didn't seem to understand the very basics of finances to begin with. When I heard them ask questions like, "Is that good?" or "Would you recommend that?" it scared the bejeesus out of me. I had to reply saying... I am not able to give financial advice I can simply tell you reasons behind what our software's outputs and how it comes to those conclusions.

It still makes me feel weird thinking about it now... especially bigger firms that would hire so many people because of quick turn around rates. shivers
No kidding. The blind leading the blind

Fun fact: Fiduciaries are paid by fees coming out of YOUR money, instead of being paid by the insurance companies they represent. This is all about the government keeping money out of retirement accounts so they can keep taxing it.
